basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens 'Vers. 21. Locutus est fratribus: Post mortem meam visitabit vos Dominus, et reliqua.'. The printing states no chapter here and the lemma is too short to match, so the chapter is the one the preceding block established.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 21. Locutus est fratribus: Post mortem meam visitabit vos Dominus, et reliqua. Joseph igitur, qui sicut pater ejus Jacob terram repromissionis tota mente desiderabat, incolatumque Aegypti detestabatur, moraliter nos instruit ut quandiu sumus in hoc mundo, semper desideremus ingredi terram repromissionis, id est terram viventium, ibique requiescere optemus. Quod tunc digne fit si numerum annorum aetatis ipsius moribus imitemur.
